submissions.notes:
Architecture
React 18 + TypeScript frontend with React Flow for real-time agent visualization. FastAPI + Python backend with 9 AI agents running concurrently via SSE streaming. Supabase Postgres with pgvector (HNSW index) for RAG over 22 embedded chunks from 13 gov.uk HMRC manual pages. OpenAI gpt-3.5-turbo for agent reasoning, text-embedding-3-small for vector embeddings

Integrations
Real HMRC sandbox OAuth (authorization code grant against test-api.service.hmrc.gov.uk). Real Xero OAuth 2.0. Both are live OAuth flows, not simulations. 28 API endpoints total.

How it works
Connect Xero (pulls financials) and HMRC (pulls obligations)
9 specialist agents run in parallel: R&D Tax Relief, Capital Allowances, VAT Scheme Optimization, Salary/Dividend, Employment Allowance, plus Profile Builder, Orchestrator, Bank Categorizer, and Tax Analysis Conductor

Each agent queries real HMRC guidance via RAG (pgvector cosine similarity search), produces findings with confidence scores (0-100%) and reasoning chains citing specific 

HMRC legislation
Items above 85% confidence are auto-approved. Below 85% are escalated to the human for review
One click files to HMRC sandbox. Receipt ID returned. Full audit trail with every agent decision, confidence score, HMRC reference, and whether it was auto-approved or human-reviewed

What judges should know
Every HMRC citation badge is clickable and opens the real gov.uk page. The RAG pipeline is real: 13 gov.uk pages scraped with BeautifulSoup, chunked at ~280 words, embedded with OpenAI, stored in pgvector, searched via cosine similarity with a 0.7 threshold. The HMRC OAuth redirects to the actual HMRC sandbox login page. This is not a wrapper around an LLM. It is a multi-agent system that makes autonomous decisions, scores its own confidence, escalates uncertainty, and files to a real government API.
Track: Financial Intelligence
Built with: React, TypeScript, Vite, FastAPI, Supabase + pgvector, OpenAI, React Flow, SSE Streaming, HMRC sandbox API, Xero OAuth, Cursor

submissions.notes:
FinIntel Agent — Track 2: Financial Intelligence

Ingest → classify → gate: every transaction hits MongoDB Atlas Local, a change-stream watcher dispatches to a DeepAgent classifier (LiteLLM routing, structured output), and a confidence gate decides auto-categorise vs. escalate.
HITL is the product: uncertain transactions (confidence < 85%) and suspicious ones (fraud score > 0.5) land in a review queue with the agent's rationale visible. Approve, mark fraud, or re-categorise — one tap.
The agent learns: human corrections are persisted via LangMem. Same merchant pattern on the next seed → higher confidence, no retraining, no redeploy.
Explain this charge: streaming plain-English explanation per transaction, backed by web search + memory retrieval.
Hybrid search: VoyageAI embeddings + Atlas Vector Search + Atlas full-text fuzzy, score-fused — natural language queries like "suspicious accommodation London" resolve correctly.
Cursor SDK bonus: src/agent/sdk.py mirrors the TypeScript SDK interface (Agent.create → Run.stream). Routes to local DeepAgent today; one config flag (CURSOR_SDK_ENABLED=true) switches to the real cloud runtime via cursor_sdk/runner.mjs.
The core question Track 2 asks — how confident is the agent really, and which edge cases deserve a human eye? — is answered with a working threshold gate, a visible rationale, and a memory loop that tightens confidence over time.

submissions.description: Mikado is the AI agent for your AP review queue - it pays the safe invoices, refuses the suspicious ones, and signs every decision.

submissions.notes:
Architecture

Gradio UI (app.py) -> Agent loop (agent.py) -> Tool layer (Tools.py) -> Specter API client (Specter.py).
The model generates a structured risk memo, then deterministic policy guardrails run post-generation to enforce safety-critical outcomes.
Output is schema-validated and rendered with evidence + tool trace for auditability.
Integration

Live Specter integration for company search and enrichment (/companies/search + /companies).
Anthropic model for reasoning and memo synthesis.
Runtime optimizations include connection reuse, warmup, and in-memory caching for faster repeated queries.
Safety & Controls

Three explicit outcomes: PROCEED, ESCALATE, DECLINE.
Unknown/unresolved entities are forced into a safe fail path.
Mixed signals and low-confidence scenarios are explicitly routed to safer decisions.
Known Gaps / Future Work

No authentication/tenant isolation yet (prototype scope).
Limited observability/analytics dashboard (currently trace-focused, not metrics-rich).
Confidence calibration is rule-assisted but not yet benchmarked on a large labeled dataset.
Deeper fallback sources beyond Specter would improve resilience when upstream coverage is thin.

submissions.notes: Sourcy is an autonomous procurement agent for B2B buyers. Tell it what you need in plain English — "find me 3 quotes for 50k boxes by Friday" or "pay all approved invoices under £10k tonight" — and it runs the full loop: sourcing, RFQ, negotiation, PO matching, and payment. What's new for the Money Movement track is that the agent actually moves the money (single-use virtual cards via Stripe Issuing for low-value spend, ACH/SWIFT for invoices, stablecoin rails scaffolded for cross-border) under hard spend caps, approval thresholds, and a full reversible audit trail — not blanket access. Team: Edward (quant at State Street, AI engineer, built the agent orchestration), Tom (stablecoin payments, founder of Xeno.Money, led the payments architecture), Phoebe (ex-Mastercard with a Pay-by-Bank patent, founder of The Behaviour Company, led product and compliance framing).
